findings.title: Missing double-check under write lock causes duplicate loads and cache replacement
findings.body: After acquiring the exclusive Lock at line 48, the code does not re-check entryPointAssetsCache. Two concurrent cold-cache callers in non-Dev mode can both pass the RLock check with ret==nil, then sequentially each perform readWebAssetsFromFile (and SetContentDeliveryURL) and overwrite entryPointAssetsCache, with the first caller returning a pointer that is no longer the cached one. This wastes I/O and can yield different EntryPointAssets instances to concurrent callers; re-checking `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after Lock and returning it would make the fast path race-free and single-load.

findings.title: Mutex only guards the pointer, shared mutable EntryPointAssets is still returned to all callers
findings.body: GetWebAssets returns the same *dtos.EntryPointAssets pointer stored in the global cache to every caller. The new RWMutex protects only reading/writing the pointer variable, not the pointed-to struct/slices. Any caller that mutates the returned value (as this function itself does via result.SetContentDeliveryURL at line 64) races with concurrent readers of the cached object. The fix is incomplete unless callers are guaranteed never to mutate the result; returning a copy/clone on the cached path (or documenting/enforcing immutability) is needed to fully eliminate the shared-global-state race described in the PR.
